meta.title: Sable Crest Ferry Emergency in Marnesh Straits
meta.subtitle: Ferry emergency | Marnesh Straits and Halvary | Undated response period

bullets.text: Marnesh Coastguard was responding to a distress call from the MV Sable Crest while emergency operations were underway.
Multiple reports confirmed damage to the ferry, and an eyewitness reported that it was lying on its side.
Rescue operations progressed from deployment and active rescue to reports that the operation was complete.
An evacuation was confirmed for Halvary and Halvary headland, including instructions for fishing crews and residents to leave or avoid the area.
Marnesh Coastguard received a distress call from the MV Sable Crest and began responding.
Search-and-rescue assets and helicopters were tasked or deployed to the scene while rescue activity was underway.
Evacuation notices were issued for Halvary and Halvary headland during the response.
Coastguard updates reported that 96 people had been recovered from the water and brought ashore at Halvary so far.
Officials subsequently said rescue efforts at Marnesh Straits were complete and confirmed that the crew had been rescued.
Officials and other reports confirmed a rescue at the ferry or vessel without specifying how many people were involved.
The vessel's crew was reported rescued.
Coastguard updates stated that 96 people had been recovered from the water and brought ashore at Halvary.
Officials and ferry-related accounts reported confirmed damage to the vessel in Marnesh Straits.
An eyewitness account stated that the ferry was lying on its side.
A ferry-news account relayed an unverified report that Grayford was closed.
Fishing crews were instructed to evacuate Halvary or Halvary headland and avoid the area.
An immediate evacuation notice directed people, including residents, to leave Halvary or Halvary headland.
The ferry's position on its side indicated a serious hazardous condition at the vessel.
A vague report suggested that an unspecified serious problem was occurring in the straits.
Search-and-rescue assets, including helicopters from two stations, were deployed or tasked to the scene in Marnesh Straits.
Marnesh Coastguard and other responders were actively responding to the Sable Crest emergency and to Halvary.
Officials reported that rescue operations were underway before later announcing their completion.
A support point was opened near the vessel for affected people.
Local and official reports stated that unspecified help had been received in connection with the Sable Crest response.
Warnings instructed fishing crews and the public to avoid the affected area around Marnesh Straits and Halvary.
Evacuation alerts instructed people to leave Halvary or Halvary headland immediately.
Officials and ferry-related accounts circulated updates confirming damage to the vessel.
Officials and other accounts circulated successive updates that a rescue was confirmed, underway, and later complete.
Marnesh Coastguard reported that it was responding to the Sable Crest distress call.
Multiple accounts repeated the Coastguard update that 96 people had been recovered and brought ashore at Halvary.
Two posts advertised situation updates about Halvary without supplying substantive details in their text.
A poster requested updates and an official figure for the number of vehicles on the cargo deck on behalf of family in the area.
Posts expressed concern for people near the coastguard and hoped that everyone was safe.

bullets.text: The reported closure of Grayford was based only on hearsay and lacked official confirmation.
A post suggested that something was seriously wrong in the straits without identifying a specific event or source.
No tweet reports confirmed fatalities, injuries, trapped people, or missing people.
The cause of the Sable Crest's distress and reported damage is not stated.
No official figure was available for the number of vehicles on the cargo deck.
The recovery count of 96 was explicitly provisional and no final total was provided.
Reports that help was received did not identify the recipient or the assistance provided.
Posts referring to a situation update about Halvary did not include the substance of that update.
Fifteen signal tweets explicitly attributed information to officials or Marnesh Coastguard sources.
Nineteen signal tweets were retweets, indicating substantial secondary recirculation of crisis information.
One signal tweet explicitly presented its report as an eyewitness account.
Seven signal tweets used hearsay or reporting cues without clear official attribution in their own text.
Retweets accounted for 19 of the 41 signal tweets.
The Coastguard recovery figure of 96 people was repeated across three posts and multiple accounts.
The Halvary evacuation message was repeated across eight posts with closely matching instructions.
Reports of vessel damage were repeated across four posts from official and ferry-related accounts.
Rescue-status information was repeated across eight posts as confirmation, active-operation, and completion updates.
